summary.oneLiner: Orient Technologies delivered 22.25% YoY revenue growth in Q2FY26 driven by large government and BFSI deals, with strategic investments in SOC and DaaS nearing monetization; the upcoming commercialization of its cybersecurity SOC in Q4FY26 is the key catalyst for margin expansion and recurring revenue scaling.

one-line thesis: Orient Technologies delivered 22.25% YoY revenue growth in Q2FY26 driven by large government and BFSI deals, with strategic investments in SOC and DaaS nearing monetization; the upcoming commercialization of its cybersecurity SOC in Q4FY26 is the key catalyst for margin expansion and recurring revenue scaling.
financial scorecard: revenue: +22.25% YoY to Rs.272.80cr; EBITDA/margin: Rs.21.96cr (8.05% margin) - impacted by Rs.2.5cr SOC setup costs; PAT (rptd): +24.5% YoY to Rs.14.17cr; PAT (normalized): ~Rs.16.5cr (ex-SOC capex amortization); order book: Rs.30.81cr (New India Assurance) + Rs.30cr (Big Four) + Rs.3.75cr (pharma) + Rs.18.69cr (Maharashtra VAT); net debt: net cash position (IPO proceeds used for SOC capex)
guidance: revenue growth: solid double-digit for FY26; margin: gradual improvement from Q4FY26 as SOC scales; order inflow: strong pipeline in BFSI, PSU, and cloud; capex/commissioning: SOC and Navi Mumbai center fully built, now in monetization phase
order book & pipeline: Rs.30.81cr (New India Assurance, multi-year); Rs.30cr (Big Four consulting, tech refresh); Rs.3.75cr (global pharma, Azure Stack); Rs.18.69cr (Maharashtra VAT automation, 5-year)
segment / subsidiary detail: Telecom: 13.11%; BFSI: 14.90%; Government/PSU: 19.65%; ITES: 4.94%; Mid-market & others (healthcare, manufacturing, logistics, etc.): 47.40%
growth verticals / optionality: Expansion into Total Outsourcing Service (ToS) bundling infrastructure + application management; potential cross-border reference wins from foreign bank deal; AI-enabled automation services as production use cases emerge
margins & cost dynamics: EBITDA margin compressed in H1FY26 due to Rs.2.5cr SOC setup costs (fully expensed); margin to improve from Q4FY26 as SOC revenue ramps and annuity contracts scale; no new capex planned beyond existing SOC and Navi Mumbai center
capex / expansion: Rs.10cr from IPO used for premises; Rs.2.5cr for SOC tools/equipment; total capex of Rs.12.5cr fully incurred; no further capex planned for FY26
capital allocation: All capex funded via IPO proceeds; no debt raised; no dividends or buybacks mentioned; future allocation focused on scaling SOC and ToS offerings, not M&A
risks & watch-items: Delayed premises handover for SOC (2-month delay); slow enterprise adoption of AI due to ROI uncertainty; reliance on domestic market (no international revenue yet); execution risk in scaling 24x7 operations at Navi Mumbai center
management quality / tone: Confident and execution-focused; strong emphasis on operational readiness of SOC and DaaS; avoids forward-looking guidance but signals clear monetization timeline; proud of government and BFSI wins; acknowledges AI hype but stresses practical use cases
non-obvious takeaways: The Rs.30.81cr New India Assurance deal is not just a one-off — it’s a multi-year recurring revenue anchor that validates the PSU digitalization play; SOC is not a cost center but a recurring service engine with proven pipeline, not yet reflected in P&L
challenges → beneficiaries & losers:
| Challenge | Beneficiary/Loser | Dir | Conviction | Note |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Customers hesitant to adopt AI due to unclear ROI | Orient Technologies Limited | beneficiary | High | As AI moves from POC to production, Orient's managed services and automation expertise position it to capture high-margin follow-on contracts |
| Competitors focused on software-only SaaS | Orient Technologies Limited | beneficiary | High | Orient's DaaS + ToS model (infrastructure + application management) creates sticky, higher-margin customer relationships vs. pure-play SaaS vendors |

themes.title: AI-led IT services & ER&D transformation
themes.need: Q1FY27 split the bucket three ways: a soft large-cap core, a re-accelerating mid-cap tier, and an outright business-model change. TCS grew constant currency only +0.4% QoQ / +3.2% YoY despite $9.5bn of TCV (including an ~$800mn net-new SKF mega-deal), and its AI-services book annualising $2.6bn (+13.6% QoQ) saw incremental adds DECELERATE from +$125mn to +$75mn - AI is still project revenue, not annuity. WIPRO is the laggard (+0.9% YoY cc, margin -120bps to 16.0%, Q2 guided -1.5% to +0.5%). Mid-caps are outgrowing: TECHM grew +6.6% YoY cc with every vertical up and an 11th consecutive quarter of margin expansion (14.4%, +330bps); MPHASIS's pipeline is at an all-time high, 2.8x its size at the Mphasis.ai launch and +28% YoY, with AI-led deals now 70% of it (from 12%) and BFS pipeline +100% YoY, and its new Tria platform closed multiple opportunities within seven weeks of launch; FRACTAL lifted net income +92% YoY on INR 912.5cr revenue at NRR 117% with zero churn (though only +9% cc, dragged by TMT -22%); KPITTECH won $349M of new deals with 21% of pipeline now productized AI/SDV solutions. Structurally, HCLTECH is entering the AI-datacenter business with an initial investment of up to INR 3,500cr and a 50MW long-term ambition, and PERSISTENT is buying Nagarro at EUR 1.27bn EV to build a $2.9bn / 46,000-person group - European scale is now bought, not built. The new cost line is visas: TATAELXSI crossed INR 1,000cr of quarterly revenue for the first time (INR 1,021.1cr) yet EBIT fell 330bps QoQ, with 220-230bps of it onsite/subcontractor investment the CFO said cannot be passed to customers.
themes.driver: MPHASIS's guide that 'Q2 is positioned to deliver the best sequential constant currency growth we have delivered in three years' is the most falsifiable claim in the sector; then HCLTECH's AI-datacenter build, the PERSISTENT-Nagarro close, and whether TCS's AI incremental adds re-accelerate off +$75mn.

business_model.title: Positioning (investor deck)
business_model.body:
- Tagline positioning is "Empowering enterprises to scale, secure, and transform with reliable IT infrastructure, managed services, and digital innovation — all under one roof", with the sales promise "Bringing end-to-end IT under one SLA – so you can focus on growth".
- Capability build-out is presented as a staged 25+ year progression: founded 1997 selling computers and telefax machines; 1999 OEM partnerships for Data Centre Solutions; 2006 Managed Services; 2013 Cloud Services; 2017 Digital Transformation (RPA, BI, mobile & web apps, facility management); 2023 ESG under Sustainability Services; 2024 listing plus Cybersecurity & Digital Forensics and Remote Infrastructure Management (RIM).
- Customer base is described as "marquee" and diversified, attributed to "our ability to tailor and customise our product and services to suit the requirements of our customers"; Q1 2026-2027 industry-wise revenue share is BFSI 24.92%, ITES 16.82%, Government & PSU 12.29%, Telecommunication 1.92% and Mid-market & Others 44.06% (the last defined as healthcare, manufacturing, infrastructure, real estate, logistics, education, e-commerce, conglomerates, energy and service industries).
- Dell International Services India Pvt. Ltd. is named on the Tech Partners panel.

other.title: Notable from the deck
other.body:
- [Order book] Order Book of Rs 375.43 crore as of 12th August 2026, billable during FY27.
- [Key wins] Q1 wins include a Rs 20 crore engagement with a leading public-sector insurance company and a Rs 24 crore cloud engagement with a leading general insurance company, described as strengthening presence across insurance, cloud services and BFSI.
- [Geographic concentration] "Our Company's business operations are concentrated in India & its revenue is predominantly generated from India. The Company aims to expand their geographic footprint and cater to a broader customer base globally."
- [Industry TAM, CRISIL] All market-size and CAGR figures come from a Company-commissioned CRISIL report titled 'Analysis of IT Services, Cloud Computing and Data Centre in India' dated July 2024; headline Indian IT industry ~$246 Billion, split as IT Services ~$129 Billion, ITeS ~$45 Billion, Software Products and ER&D ~$54 Billion, Hardware ~$18 Billion.
- [Fastest-growing addressed markets] Per the same CRISIL report, India's Data Centre industry is projected at a FY23-27P CAGR of 30-35% (Rs 84.5 Bn to Rs 240-280 Bn) and Public Cloud Services at 22-28% (Rs 550 Bn to Rs 1,250-1,450 Bn) — the two fastest-growing of the markets the Company addresses.
